home.title: Gaming performance toolkit
home.performanceControlDesc: Set power settings and fan speeds to balance heat, noise and performance.
home.unlimitedDesc: Advanced manual control of power and temperature settings.
home.advancedTuningDesc: Increase your system's performance with advanced optimization and overclocking for your CPU and GPU.
home.graphicsSwitcherDesc: Choose which GPU your system uses to save battery or maximise performance.
home.networkBoosterDesc: Control home network traffic to prioritise your game.
home.autoEcoHint: Unplugging drops to Balanced; a machine that stays idle, or whose battery gets low, goes on to Eco.
home.autoPerformanceHint: Plugging in steps up to Performance; an idle machine on mains comes back down to Balanced. Unlimited is never chosen for you.
home.fanCleaningDesc: Spin the fans backwards for a few seconds to shake dust out of the vents.
home.thermalBackOff: Step down when it runs hot
home.thermalBackOffHint: A machine over 85 °C drops to the quieter profile until it is back under 75 °C. Two thresholds rather than one, so it does not flip back into the same wall a degree later. Outranks the other two rules - heat and load always arrive together.
home.runningHot: Running hot: the automatic switch is holding the machine at the quieter profile.

vitals.gpuTempUnavailable: This chip publishes no temperature sensor; the kernel exposes none for it.
vitals.legendGreen: Green: low to moderate CPU/GPU temperature
vitals.legendRed: Red: critical CPU/GPU temperature. If it stays there, check your cooling.

performance.warning: Performance settings are overridden by system defaults when running on battery or on a low-power AC adapter. Your system's performance returns to normal once a compatible AC adapter is connected.
performance.applyToOsPowerProfile: Apply to the OS power profile

modeDesc.eco: Lowest power draw and the quietest fans. Best for battery life.
modeDesc.balanced: The firmware decides. Good default for everyday use.
modeDesc.performance: Higher power limits and a more aggressive fan curve.
modeDesc.unlimited: Unlocks manual power limits and manual fan control.

performance.fanCurveDesc: Drag the points to set the fan speed for each temperature.
performance.fanSpeedUnavailable: This machine's driver can switch the fans between automatic and maximum, but cannot set a speed: it exposes pwm1_enable and no pwm1. Run the hardware check for the details.
performance.turboHint: Lets the CPU burst above its base frequency. Turning it off is the single biggest thing you can do for fan noise and battery life.
performance.noPowerControl: This machine exposes no power-mode control, so the modes below are display only.
performance.autoPaused: Automatic switching paused for {seconds} s after your manual change.
performance.applyToOsProfileHint: Mirrors the selected mode onto the OS power profile (power-profiles-daemon / platform_profile), so applications that read it stay in sync.
performance.pl1Hint: Sustained CPU power limit, in watts. This is the one the fans feel.
performance.smartBoostHint: Extra wattage the firmware may add on top of the base limit.
performance.curveSensorHint: Which temperature the curve is read at. The GPU is usually what heats up first under a game; while the card is asleep the curve follows the CPU instead.
performance.curveSensorAsleep: The graphics card is reporting nothing right now, so the curve is following the CPU.
performance.limitsApplyNow: This is the mode the machine is in, so changes take effect straight away.
performance.limitsApplyLater: The machine is not in {mode} right now, so these take effect when it next switches to it.

advanced.clockLockHint: Pins the GPU between two frequencies it already supports. Not an overclock - the card never runs faster than it was shipped able to - but it stops the driver dropping the clock when you would rather it did not. Needs the daemon to be running as root.
advanced.disclaimer: Overclocking can make your system unstable and may void your warranty. Changes are not applied until you press Apply.
advanced.consentText: Overclocking runs this GPU outside the settings it was shipped with. An offset that survives a benchmark can still hang the machine in a game, and when it does there is no error message: the screen stops, and anything unsaved is gone. Nothing here is covered by the manufacturer's warranty. Every change is reverted automatically unless you confirm it, and none is restored after a reboot unless you ask for that separately.
advanced.consentTitle: Read this before you change anything
advanced.pending: Keep these settings? They are undone in {seconds} s if you say nothing.
advanced.holdHint: Changes are applied in small steps and undone automatically after {seconds} s unless you confirm them. If the machine stops responding, the daemon puts the card back on its own.
advanced.restoreOnStartHint: Off by default. A bad offset restored at boot can stop the machine reaching a desktop, so this is never assumed - and it is skipped anyway after a boot that followed a change nobody confirmed.
advanced.unconfirmedAtStart: The last change to a GPU was never confirmed, so nothing was restored on this boot and the cards are at the clocks the firmware shipped.

cleaning.title: Fan cleaning
cleaning.lead: Spins the fans backwards for a few seconds so that dust drawn into the vents is pushed back out. The same thing the OMEN Gaming Hub does under Windows, driven through the firmware rather than the fan driver.
cleaning.warningTitle: The fans stop cooling while this runs
cleaning.warningBody: A cycle reverses the fans, so nothing is being cooled until it ends. It stops on its own after the time set below, and it will not start at all above {limit}. Close anything demanding first, and expect it to be loud.
cleaning.runningHint: The fans are running backwards. This ends on its own; the button below ends it now and ramps them back to the mode they were in.
cleaning.transitioningHint: The blades are being brought to a stop, or ramped back down out of reverse. Neither is instant, and interrupting it is what the ramp exists to avoid.
cleaning.notAsked: The firmware was not asked, so nothing is known about this machine's fan cleaner yet. That is a missing kernel module or a daemon without root - not a verdict on your laptop. The Hardware check page has both fixes.
cleaning.notCapable: The firmware was asked and this machine has no fan cleaner. Most models do not.
cleaning.tooHot: The CPU is at {temp}, above the {limit} a cycle will start below. Let it cool and try again.
cleaning.durationHint: How long the fans stay reversed. The vendor's own tool uses 30 seconds, and the daemon enforces this three separate ways so a cycle cannot outlive it.
cleaning.customSpeedHint: Off means the speed your firmware has configured for itself, which is what the OMEN Gaming Hub would send. On lets you set it - lower is quieter and gentler, higher shifts more dust.

lighting.title: Lighting
lighting.lead: The four-zone light strip along the front edge, driven through the firmware over ACPI. Colours and a brightness are all the protocol carries, so there are no breathing or wave effects here - a switch that did nothing would be worse than no switch.
lighting.colourHint: Applied when you close the picker.
lighting.selectZone: Click a zone in the strip above to aim the colour picker at it.
lighting.staticHint: All four zones take the same colour. Switch to “Per zone” to set them apart.
lighting.restoreOnStartHint: Off by default: turning a machine's lights on at boot because they were on last week is your decision, not the daemon's. On, the daemon re-sends these colours when it starts.
lighting.readBackHint: Asks the firmware for the four zone colours - four ACPI round trips, so it is a button rather than a poll. It is also the only check that the payload was understood rather than merely accepted.
lighting.owned: These colours were set by this daemon.
lighting.notOwned: Nothing has been written yet, so the strip is showing whatever the firmware chose.
lighting.perKeyPresent: An HP Gaming Keyboard II (per-key RGB) is attached. It is a different device on a different bus, and this build does not drive it - these controls are the light strip only.
lighting.notSaved: The colours were sent but could not be saved, so they will not come back on a restart: {error}
lighting.noWmi: This machine has no hp-wmi interface, so there is nothing to ask about a light strip.
lighting.refused: The firmware was asked in all three protocols and refused each one, so this machine has no lighting these protocols reach.
lighting.notInstalled: The acpi_call kernel module is not installed, so the firmware cannot be asked. This is not a verdict on your laptop: install the package for your distribution, then use “Probe again”.
lighting.notLoaded: acpi_call is installed but not loaded. “sudo modprobe acpi_call”, then “Probe again”.
lighting.unreachable: /proc/acpi/call is here but could not be used, so the firmware was never asked. This is almost always a daemon without root rather than anything about the hardware.
lighting.protocolLead: There is no single OMEN lighting protocol. Three unrelated ways of talking to these lights exist, and which one a laptop speaks is not decided by its model name — so all three are tried and the first that answers is used.
lighting.dialectHint: Automatic uses the first protocol that answers a read. Pick one by hand when the automatic choice is wrong: a pinned protocol is used whether or not it answered, because you can see the lights and this app can only ask.
lighting.wrongDialect: Your firmware has a lighting command, and none of the three protocols this build knows is the one it wants. That is a machine with lights this app cannot speak to yet, not a machine without them — pinning a protocol by hand below is the next thing to try.
lighting.zoneFourUnreadable: Zone 4 always reads back black on this protocol. The colour sent to it is real — the lights show it — but acpi_call cuts the firmware's reply short one byte before zone 4 begins, so it cannot be read back. Installing a kernel driver that publishes the zones as files removes the limit.

graphics.title: Select a GPU mode
graphics.hybridDesc: Uses integrated or discrete graphics depending on the application.
graphics.integratedDesc: Disables the discrete GPU and uses only integrated graphics to maximise battery life.
graphics.discreteDesc: Best for games and graphics-heavy applications. May increase noise and heat.
graphics.rebootNeeded: Switching GPU mode requires signing out or rebooting.

network.descOff: Monitors your network bandwidth usage across every running application.
network.descAuto: Automatically prioritises the foreground application as HIGH and every other application as LOW. Select Custom to set priorities manually.
network.descCustom: Manually adjust each application's priority level or block its network access. The default value is Medium.
network.doubleForceHint: Applies the priority rules to already-established connections too.

keys.selectKey: Select a key to get started:
keys.pressKey: Press the physical key to remap
keys.testHint: Click here to test the key mapping
keys.emptyHint: Select a key above to assign it

drivers.title: Drivers
drivers.hpWmiDesc: Adds manual fan control (pwm1 / pwm1_enable) to the in-kernel hp-wmi driver. Required for anything beyond read-only monitoring.
drivers.daemonDesc: Privileged background service that talks to the hardware on behalf of this app.
drivers.acpiCallDesc: Required only by the fan cleaner (reverse spin) feature.
drivers.needsRoot: Installing asks for your password once.

notices.driverMissingBody: The patched hp-wmi driver was not found, so fan and power control are unavailable. Only read-only monitoring works.
notices.daemonDownBody: Showing simulated data. Start the daemon to control your hardware.
notices.unsupportedBody: This does not look like an HP OMEN or Victus laptop. The app runs, but hardware control will not work.

settings.title: Settings
settings.servicesHint: The daemon runs as root and is started by systemd at boot, so the fan curve and the performance key work before anyone logs in. The widget draws on your screen, so it runs in your session — Pyren starts it when it opens.
settings.widgetHint: The shortcut opens the widget; you pick a mode by clicking it. One switch for both.
settings.shortcutHint: Heard by the daemon itself, so it works on any desktop and at the login screen.
settings.shortcutTimedOut: No key arrived. Some laptops keep Fn+P to themselves and never tell Linux about it — pick an ordinary combination instead, such as Ctrl+Alt+P.
settings.widgetPreviewHint: Shows the widget without changing the power mode.
settings.widgetAtLogin: Start the widget at login, without opening Pyren
settings.demoMode: Demo data when the daemon is unreachable
settings.permissionsHint: Running the daemon as root, membership of the socket's group and the privileged readings are managed on the hardware check page — they need authentication, so they are actions rather than switches.
settings.configRecovered: Your settings file could not be read and defaults were loaded. The previous file was kept at {backup}.
settings.configTooNew: Your settings file was written by a newer version (v{found}) and was left untouched; defaults are in use for this session.
settings.configSaveFailed: Settings could not be written to disk, so changes will be lost on restart: {error}
settings.restoreOnStart: Restore the power mode when the daemon starts
settings.restoreOnStartHint: Off by default: changing the machine's power behaviour at boot should be something you asked for.

help.title: Help & about
help.aboutBody: Pyren is a free, community-built clone of HP's OMEN Gaming Hub for Linux. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by HP Inc.
help.upToDate: You are on the latest version.
help.translationsBody: Copy app/src/lib/i18n/locales/en.json, translate the values, save it as <iso>.json in the same folder and open a pull request. The language appears in Settings automatically.
help.legalBody: OMEN and the OMEN logo are trademarks of HP Inc. This project uses no HP code or assets. Provided as is, with no warranty; controlling fans and power limits carries a risk of overheating or hardware damage and is your responsibility.

reason.monitoringOnly: the hp-wmi interface is present but nothing here accepted control; fan speeds and temperatures can still be read
reason.unsupported: no hp-wmi interface and no power-mode mechanism; monitoring works, hardware control does not

acpi.notLoaded: the acpi_call kernel module is not loaded, so {path} does not exist; {hint}

dialect.refused: the firmware refused this lighting protocol (it answered: {answer})
dialect.unreadable: the firmware answered {answer}, which is not a colour reply
dialect.needsRoot: writing the kernel's zone files needs root

err.zonesRequired: params.zones is required: four colours, '#rrggbb' or [r, g, b]
err.colorRequired: params.color is required: '#rrggbb' or [r, g, b]
err.dialectRequired: params.dialect is required: 'auto', or one of the ids in getCapabilities
err.dialectUnknown: there is no lighting dialect called {got}

diagnostics.allowWrites: Also test that the fan accepts writes
diagnostics.allowWritesHint: Rewrites the value already set and restores the previous mode, so no fan changes speed. Needs the daemon to be running as root.

verdict.monitoringOnly: Monitoring only — fan speed cannot be set
verdict.unsupported: No fan-control interface on this machine

checks.notANumberAt: {path} contains something that is not a number

hp-wmi.title: hp-wmi platform driver
hp-wmi.remedy: This is normal on non-HP hardware. On an HP laptop, check that the hp_wmi module is loaded (`modprobe hp_wmi`) and that the BIOS exposes WMI.

fan.reverse: {raw} raw -> {actual} rpm, spinning in reverse (fan cleaner active)

pwm1.notExposed: pwm1 is not exposed, so fan speed cannot be set
pwm1.remedyNotice: Needs a kernel whose hp-wmi supports this board (see the notice below).
pwm1.remedy: Needs a kernel whose hp-wmi supports this board.

pwm-write.title: PWM accepts writes
pwm-write.noChannel: no PWM channel to write to
pwm-write.notAttempted: not attempted; enable writes to test this
pwm-write.noMode: could not read the current mode
pwm-write.noValue: could not read the current PWM value
pwm-write.ok: wrote and read back pwm1 = {value} without changing fan speed
pwm-write.mismatch: wrote {wrote} but read back {readback}; the driver may quantise or ignore values

kernel-log.title: hp-wmi kernel messages
kernel-log.notReadable: kernel log not readable; run as root, or paste `dmesg | grep -i hp.wmi`
kernel-log.selfBuilt: Nothing wrong here. The 'module verification failed' line is the kernel noting that a module built outside your distribution's kernel package was loaded, and tainting itself to record that - which is exactly what installing the patched hp-wmi does, so it is expected rather than a fault: {lines}

platform-profile.title: ACPI platform profile
platform-profile.absent: not exposed; power modes fall back to power-profiles-daemon or the CPU EPP hint

acpi-call.title: acpi_call module
acpi-call.absent: /proc/acpi/call not found; the RGB lightbar and the fan cleaner both need it
acpi-call.remedy: Install acpi_call-dkms (Arch), acpi-call-dkms (Debian) or akmod-acpi_call (Fedora), then `modprobe acpi_call`.

fan-cleaner.title: Fan cleaner (reverse spin)
fan-cleaner.remedyAsk: The firmware is asked over {path}, which needs the acpi_call module loaded and root to write. With both, run this again.

diagnostics.neverRun: The check has not been run yet.
diagnostics.cliHint: The same check runs without the app: cargo run -p pyren-check (add --json for a bug report).
diagnostics.wroteToHardware: This run wrote to the hardware and restored the previous state.

summary.fullControlTested: Fan control works: speeds can be read and the PWM channel accepted a write.
summary.fullControlUntested: Fan control looks available: the PWM channel is present. Re-run with writes enabled to confirm the hardware accepts them.
summary.monitoringOnly: Fan speeds can be read, but this driver exposes no PWM channel, so speed cannot be set.
summary.unsupportedWithTemp: This machine exposes no HP fan-control interface. Temperature can still be read, so monitoring works.
summary.unsupportedNoTemp: This machine exposes no HP fan-control interface. No HP fan interface and no usable temperature sensor were found.

driverNotice.noPwm: The kernel's hp-wmi has no pwm1 for this board. Recent kernels ship manual fan control upstream, so upgrading the kernel is the first thing to try. Failing that, a patched out-of-tree driver exists: {hint}. Installing it replaces a kernel module, so it is a deliberate step, not something this app does for you.
driverNotice.noHpWmi: No hp-wmi device at all. On an HP OMEN or Victus laptop, load the hp_wmi module; on other hardware this is expected and fan control is not applicable.

installer.title: Kernel driver
installer.intro: Installing the patched hp-wmi driver unloads a kernel module, replaces a file under /lib/modules and regenerates the initramfs. Nothing here runs until you have read the plan and run it as a dry run first.

verdict.needed: This machine has no manual fan control and this kernel has none of its own. The patched driver is the remedy.
verdict.works: Fan control already works here. Replacing the stock driver would be a downgrade — installing is refused unless you force it.
verdict.boardMissing: Fan control does not work here, even though this kernel ships manual fan control of its own: the stock driver came up without pwm1. That is the case where the patched driver plus this board's id in the right table can help — and the only way to know is to try it.

installer.manualHint: Fill the fields in yourself. Anything left blank keeps the driver's own value — which for the fan ceiling is a guess, and for the board table means the board is not added at all.
installer.autoHint: Works out everything an install needs from this machine — the board id from DMI, which of the driver's tables it belongs in, and the fan ceilings from the last calibration — then dry-runs the plan. Nothing is changed until you confirm.
installer.preferHooks: Build once, plus a kernel hook
installer.preferHooksHint: Use the distribution's kernel hook instead of DKMS, even where DKMS is available.
installer.forceHint: Proceed even where fan control already works, or where the hardware is not a recognised HP gaming laptop. Rarely the right answer.
installer.maxRpmHint: The RPM the driver should treat as full speed. Left blank, it keeps its own fallback — which is a guess. Run the fan calibration first to measure it.
installer.maxRpmMeasured: Calibration measured {rpm} rpm on this machine.
installer.boardHint: Adds this board id to one of the driver's tables. The table decides which EC offset the driver reads for the thermal profile, so the wrong one gives a driver that loads and then misreads the hardware.
installer.dryRunFirst: Run it as a dry run first: applying stays disabled until the exact plan above has been run without touching anything.
installer.stepsHint: Optional steps can be switched off — the plan tolerates them failing, so it can do without them. Everything else has to run, and has no switch.
installer.internalStep: carried out by the daemon itself
installer.dryRunReport: Dry run — what would have happened

afterInstall.working: It worked — pwm1 is there, so the patched module is the one in use. One step is left: the daemon looked for its fan paths when it started, before pwm1 existed, so it still reports that a speed cannot be set. Restart it (or reboot) and the fan page can command a speed:
afterInstall.needsReload: The patched module is installed on disk, but pwm1 is still missing — the kernel is very likely still running the module it loaded at boot, because it could not be unloaded while something was using it. Reboot, or run this and reopen this page:
afterInstall.ifStillNothing: If pwm1 is still missing after a reboot, the module loaded but this board's firmware did not answer the fan query. Nothing is broken and nothing is left behind: "Restore stock driver" puts back the module that was backed up during the install.
afterInstall.restored: The stock module is back on disk. Reboot, or run this, for the kernel to actually go back to it:

step.patch-source: Patch the staged source under {path} (fan ceilings, and any experimental board id)
step.stage-source: Copy the driver sources and dkms.conf to {path}
step.backup-driver: Back up the stock hp-wmi.ko next to itself as .bak, then remove it so depmod picks the new one unambiguously
step.dkms-remove-old: Remove the previously registered DKMS module
step.make: Build the module for the running kernel
step.install-hook-pacman: Install the pacman hook that rebuilds the module on kernel upgrades
step.install-hook-postinst: Install the /etc/kernel/postinst.d hook that rebuilds on kernel upgrades
step.install-hook-kernel-install: Install the /etc/kernel/install.d hook that rebuilds on kernel upgrades
step.restore-backups: Rename every hp-wmi.ko.bak back to hp-wmi.ko, restoring the stock driver
step.create-group: Create the '{group}' group that may reach the daemon
step.enable: Enable and start the daemon at boot
step.disable: Stop the daemon and remove it from boot

warn.alreadyInstalled: Fan control works here because the patched driver is already installed. Reinstalling rebuilds and reinstates it, which is what a kernel upgrade needs if no hook rebuilt it automatically. To go back to the distribution's own driver, use "restore" instead.
warn.alreadyWorks: Fan control already works on this machine (pwm1 is present) and it is not this installer's doing, so the stock driver supports this board and the patched one would add nothing.
warn.noHook: This distribution has no recognised kernel-hook mechanism, so the module will be built for the running kernel only and will need reinstalling after a kernel upgrade.
warn.serviceInstalled: The service unit is already installed; it will be replaced.
warn.joinGroup: Add each user who should control this machine to the '{group}' group: sudo usermod -aG {group} $USER (then log out and back in).
warn.boardMissing: Kernel {kernel} ships manual fan control upstream (since {major}.{minor}), and hp-wmi is loaded here - yet there is no pwm1. The stock driver did not recognise this board, which is exactly the case the patched driver plus your board's id in the right table exists for. Whether the firmware then honours a fan write is something only trying it can answer.
warn.noHpWmi: Kernel {kernel} ships manual fan control upstream (since {major}.{minor}), but hp-wmi is not loaded at all here, so there is nothing to say this is one of the laptops either driver is for. Installing is unlikely to help.

blocker.alreadyWorking: Fan control is already available; nothing to install.
blocker.noDriverSource: The patched hp-wmi sources were not found. Pyren ships them in its own driver/ directory; a packaged build has to install that to /usr/share/pyren/driver, or PYREN_DRIVER_DIR has to point at a copy.
blocker.kernelHeaders: Kernel headers for the running kernel are missing or incomplete, so the module cannot be compiled.
blocker.buildTools: A C compiler and make are required to build the module.

exec.internalAction: carried out by the daemon itself

auto.noBoardId: This machine's firmware does not publish a DMI board name, so no board can be added to the driver's tables.
auto.noDriverSource: Board {board} was found, but without the driver sources there is no way to tell whether the driver already lists it.
auto.boardKnown: Board {board} is already in the driver's feature table, so no board patch is needed.
auto.boardNew: Board {board} is not in the driver's feature table; it will be added with the {params} parameters.
auto.unknownFamily: Board {board} is not in the driver's tables, and this machine does not identify itself as an OMEN or a Victus, so which parameters it wants cannot be guessed. Choose them by hand below.
auto.rpmCalibrated: Fan ceilings taken from the last calibration run: {cpu} (CPU), {gpu} (GPU).
auto.rpmNotCalibrated: No fan calibration has been run here, so the driver keeps its own ceiling - it asks the firmware for one first, and only falls back to a compiled-in number if that fails. Run the fan calibration and install again to pin down measured values.
auto.paramsInert: This choice does not affect this board. It is already in the driver's {table}, so the driver takes that thermal-profile path and never reads the variant's own EC offset - and all four variants share one fan profile, so none of them changes fan control either.
auto.paramsVictus: Victus boards have one parameter set in this driver, and upstream marks its EC offset unknown - so the thermal profile is remembered rather than read back. Nothing to measure.
auto.paramsMeasuredOmen: Measured, not guessed: EC offset 0x95 is holding a value the OMEN thermal profile uses, so that is where this board keeps it. omen_v1_legacy is the variant that reads there.
auto.paramsMeasuredVictusS: Measured, not guessed: EC offset 0x59 is holding a value the OMEN thermal profile uses, so that is where this board keeps it. omen_v1 is the variant that reads there.
auto.paramsNoOffset: The embedded controller was read and holds a thermal profile at neither offset the driver knows, so this board keeps it somewhere else. omen_v1_no_ec is the variant that reads none - which is the right answer here, not a fallback: the driver remembers the profile it set instead.
auto.paramsUnmeasured: The embedded controller could not be read, so which EC offset holds the thermal profile is unknown. omen_v1_no_ec reads none of them, which is the safe half of that choice - the driver remembers the profile it set. Only the readback is affected; setting a profile goes over WMI either way.

admin.title: Permissions
admin.intro: What Pyren is allowed to do on this machine. Most of what looks like broken hardware is a missing privilege, and from the app the two look the same.
admin.noPolkit: No polkit agent was found, so these cannot be fixed from here. The commands are in docs/02-development.md.
admin.serviceInstallable: Not installed. Installing it makes the daemon run as root under systemd, which is what unlocks the privileged readings — and it survives reboots. Uses {binary}.
admin.serviceNoBinary: No systemd unit installed, and the pyren-daemon binary could not be found. Build or install it first, or point PYREN_DAEMON at it.
admin.groupMissing: Your user is not in '{group}', so the daemon's socket refuses the connection.
admin.groupNeedsRelogin: The group has been granted, but this login session still carries the groups it started with. Log out and back in to finish.
admin.socketDenied: {path} exists but refuses this user - that is the group above.
admin.perfOk: Available: the daemon can read Intel engine utilisation.
admin.perfNotRoot: Unavailable: reading Intel engine utilisation needs CAP_PERFMON, which the daemon gets by running as root under systemd.
admin.perfNoIntel: Not applicable: this machine has no Intel GPU with a perf PMU.
admin.perfUnknown: Unknown until the daemon can be reached.
admin.rootOk: Running as root, so every reading is available.
admin.rootNo: Running unprivileged. Readings that need root — integrated-GPU utilisation — are unavailable. Install the service above to fix this permanently.
admin.rootShadowed: A privileged service is installed and running, but the app is connected to a different, unprivileged daemon on {path}. Stop that one — and if the group row above asks you to log out, do that first, since the service's socket is only reachable with the group.
admin.rootUnknown: Unknown until the daemon can be reached.
admin.acpiCallOk: /proc/acpi/call is available, so the fan cleaner and the lightbar can reach the firmware.
admin.acpiCallNotLoaded: installed but not loaded. Loading it also arranges for it to load at boot.
admin.acpiCallMissing: not built for this kernel. Install acpi_call-dkms (Arch), acpi-call-dkms (Debian/Ubuntu) or akmod-acpi_call (Fedora), then come back here.

clamp.coreOutOfRange: core offset {requested} MHz is outside what the driver advertises ({min} to {max} MHz); using {used} MHz
clamp.noCoreOffset: this GPU exposes no core-clock offset, so that part was ignored
clamp.memOutOfRange: memory offset {requested} MHz is outside what the driver advertises ({min} to {max} MHz); using {used} MHz
clamp.noMemOffset: this GPU exposes no memory offset, so that part was ignored
clamp.lockOutOfRange: clock lock {reqMin}-{reqMax} MHz is outside what this GPU supports ({min} to {max} MHz); using {usedMin}-{usedMax} MHz
clamp.noClockLock: this GPU cannot have its clocks pinned, so that part was ignored

probe.noGpu: no GPU was found to ask about
probe.nothingTunable: a GPU was found, and nothing about it can be changed on this machine

gpu.unknownDriver: no tuning interface is known for the {driver} driver

settable.lock: Clock offsets can be set. Clocks can be pinned between {min} and {max} MHz, which needs root and stays inside what the card already supports.
settable.ceiling: Clock offsets can be set. The card reports a maximum of {mhz} MHz and will not enumerate the clocks it supports, so pinning them is not offered.
settable.noLock: Clock offsets can be set. This card's clocks cannot be pinned.

coolbits.lock: Clock offsets are readable but not settable; the X screen needs Coolbits before the driver will take one. Clocks can be pinned between {min} and {max} MHz, which needs root and stays inside what the card already supports.
coolbits.ceiling: Clock offsets are readable but not settable; the X screen needs Coolbits before the driver will take one. The card reports a maximum of {mhz} MHz and will not enumerate the clocks it supports, so pinning them is not offered.
coolbits.noLock: Clock offsets are readable but not settable; the X screen needs Coolbits before the driver will take one. This card's clocks cannot be pinned.

readable.lock: Clock offsets are readable. Clocks can be pinned between {min} and {max} MHz, which needs root and stays inside what the card already supports.
readable.ceiling: Clock offsets are readable. The card reports a maximum of {mhz} MHz and will not enumerate the clocks it supports, so pinning them is not offered.
readable.noLock: Clock offsets are readable. This card's clocks cannot be pinned.

amd.overdriveOn: AMD Overdrive is enabled on this card and pyren does not drive it yet: it has never been tested on AMD hardware, and an untested write here is not the kind that fails with an error message
amd.overdriveOff: this card exposes pp_od_clk_voltage without an OD_SCLK table, so Overdrive is off (amdgpu.ppfeaturemask enables it)
amd.noInterface: no pp_od_clk_voltage on this card, so the kernel is offering no Overdrive interface at all

intel.ceiling: Intel graphics expose a frequency ceiling ({mhz} MHz here), not an offset: it cannot be raised above what the chip already runs at, so there is nothing on this card to overclock
intel.ceilingUnknown: Intel graphics expose a frequency ceiling, not an offset, and this kernel publishes no maximum for it

nvidia.noSocket: nvidia-settings has no X display to talk to: no socket in {path}
nvidia.refused: nvidia-settings has no X display to talk to: the X server at {display} refused this process. It admits the user that owns it, and a daemon running as root is not that user - so either that user lets us in from inside their session (xhost +si:localuser:root), or PYREN_X_DISPLAY and PYREN_XAUTHORITY point us at a display we may open. There may be no cookie file to point at: a Wayland compositor's Xwayland is often started without one
nvidia.noSession: nvidia-settings has no X display to talk to: could not open {display} ({whose}). No desktop session was running when this was asked - a daemon started at boot looks before anybody has logged in - so ask again with overclock.probe now that one is up

noDisplayHint.withCookie: nvidia-settings has no X display to talk to: could not open {display} ({whose}) with {path}. A daemon running as root is not in anybody's session; point it at one with PYREN_X_DISPLAY and PYREN_XAUTHORITY, or set the offsets from a process that is already inside that session
noDisplayHint.noCookie: nvidia-settings has no X display to talk to: could not open {display} ({whose}) with no cookie file to authenticate with. A daemon running as root is not in anybody's session; point it at one with PYREN_X_DISPLAY and PYREN_XAUTHORITY, or set the offsets from a process that is already inside that session

nvidia.coolbits: {message} - this is what an X screen with no Coolbits says, and root does not change it: the screen needs Option "Coolbits" "28" in its X configuration, and a session with no X screen of its own has none to configure

note.unconfirmedAtStart: the last overclock was never confirmed, so this boot starts at stock and nothing was restored
note.backToStock: back to the clocks the firmware shipped
note.nothingToUndo: nothing to undo: this daemon has not moved these clocks
note.revertedUnconfirmed: the change to {gpu} was not confirmed, so it was undone

err.notConsented: overclocking has not been consented to on this machine; call overclock.setConsent with the text from overclock.getState first
err.pending: the last change to {gpu} is still waiting to be confirmed or undone
err.nothingPending: there is nothing waiting to be confirmed
err.verifyCore: the driver reports a core offset of {got} MHz after being asked for {asked} MHz
err.verifyMem: the driver reports a memory offset of {got} MHz after being asked for {asked} MHz
